newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Malev plans to announce plane purchase.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Malev plans to announce plane purchase.

text.p: Hungarian national airline Malev Rt plans to expand its fleet in March 1997, Gabor Peterffy, Malev's communications director, said on Tuesday.

"We are in the final stages of negotiations with one airplane manufacturer," Peterffy added. "Not much extra time is needed for an agreement -- it's just about financing now. We could have a press conference to announce a contract for the planes maybe in November."
Peterffy declined to identify the number or type of the planes but he said no wide-bodied carriers are included.
Malev's fleet currently includes 14 Boeings (six B737-200s, four B737-300s, two B737-400s and two B767-200ERs), three Fokker 70s, and 10 Tupolevs (seven Tu-154s and three Tu-134s).
"The new airplanes will enable us to remove Tupolevs from our scheduled flights and use them only for chartered flights," Peterffy said.

The airline is owned 63.9 percent by the Hungarian Privatisation and Asset Holding Co (APV Rt), 30 percent by Italian state-owned airline Alitalia, 5 percent by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Trade's investment agency SIMEST, and 1.1 percent by other interests, including Hungarian municipalities.
